name: George Washington
description: First US president, who established executive institutions and supported federal authority within the new Constitution.

axes.brief: Constitutional elections, congressional government and voluntary retirement constrained personal power.
axes.counter: The electorate excluded many adults; hostility to factions did not abolish opposition.

axes.brief: Lawful civil order and opposition to arbitrary government framed the presidency.
axes.counter: Whiskey Rebellion enforcement and slavery severely qualified personal freedom.

axes.brief: Common American allegiance and Indigenous assimilation were national priorities.
axes.counter: Religious communities received assurances of equal civic protection.

axes.brief: Immigration and settlement were nationally administered under racially restricted naturalisation.
axes.counter: The naturalisation boundary is not evidence for every modern numerical cap or refugee rule.

axes.brief: Military capability defended the frontier and federal law.
axes.counter: Neutrality and diplomacy sought to avoid entanglement in European wars.

axes.brief: Independent national judgement and avoidance of permanent foreign entanglements were explicit priorities.
axes.counter: Commerce and temporary cooperation still connected the republic internationally.

axes.brief: Private commerce coexisted with a partly public national bank and public functions.
axes.counter: The bank did not imply public ownership of every ordinary business.

axes.brief: Federal tariffs raised revenue and supported aspects of Hamiltonian development.
axes.counter: Foreign commerce remained desirable; revenue tariffs differ from complete protection.

axes.brief: Private production coexisted with public credit, monetary institutions and strategic development.
axes.counter: No comprehensive ordinary production plan was established.

axes.brief: Property and fiscal solvency took priority over modern income equalisation.
axes.counter: Public debt settlement and limited assistance are not rejection of every public payment.

axes.brief: Public morality and religion were praised while civic protection extended across faiths.
axes.counter: A national church and clerical legislative veto were not instituted.

axes.brief: Conventional family, gender and moral expectations shaped the period.
axes.counter: Political independence and republican change did not establish modern sexual or family rights.

axes.brief: Agricultural improvement and infrastructure were valued.
axes.counter: Modern AI, neural implants and embryo enhancement are distant analogies requiring qualified choices.

axes.brief: Federal taxation, national courts and military enforcement strengthened the centre.
axes.counter: States retained constitutions, ordinary policing and local powers.

axes.brief: Agricultural education and character formation coexisted with racial hierarchy and slaveholding.
axes.counter: Moral and social hierarchy are not direct evidence for inherited IQ or violent tendencies.
